To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the collaborative environment for cyber attack detection can be used in the protection of critical infrastructure from coordinated cyber attacks, that the ESPER CEP engine can be used in this environment, that the Line Fitting algorithm can be used for SYN port scan detection in the collaborative environment, and that Line Fitting is more accurate than R-SYN and exhibits better detection latencies under certain conditions.

(i) ESPER can be used to detect inter-domain port scans, (ii) the collaboration improves the detection accuracy, and (iii) the detection accuracy and latency of Line Fitting can be improved with the collaboration, but not with R-SYN.
the collaborative environment for cyber attack detection is useful in terms of detection performance, and that Line Fitting can be used to improve both detection accuracy and detection latencies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: Can we use CEP technology to design a system that protects critical infrastructure organizations from coordinated cyber attacks?
the following question: How can we protect critical infrastructures (e.g., banks, telco providers, power grids) from coordinated cyber-attacks?
developing a collaborative CEP environment that can be used to detect cyber attacks against a critical infrastructure, and to protect it from them.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our collaborative environment, in the form presented here, is a viable solution to protect critical infrastructures from coordinated cyber attacks, and in particular from inter-domain SYN port scans.
our collaborative system, based on ESPER, provides a flexible framework for detecting coordinated attacks on a critical infrastructure.
our work shows how the collaboration can be used to improve detection accuracy and detection latency of inter-domain SYN port scans.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a collaborative CEP-based system to detect inter-domain SYN port scans, which can be easily extended to other types of malicious activities.

a collaboration among a small set of organizations, each with a low link bandwidth, can achieve a higher detection rate and lower detection latencies than a collaboration involving a larger number of participants.

the collaborative environment, the algorithms and the ESPER engine are a good starting point for a collaborative cyber attack defense system that can detect attacks at a very early stage and can be deployed on a wide range of network topologies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the collaborative environment we developed can be used to detect coordinated cyber attacks against geographically dispersed organizations.
collaboration is an effective approach to protect critical infrastructures from cyber attacks.
the collaboration can improve the detection accuracy, and that the choice of the detection algorithm is critical to achieve this accuracy improvement.
